finding.title: Replace raw Color(0xFF...) literals in core/widgets with AppColors/AppTheme constants (stat_card.dart duplicates AppColors.blueNavy verbatim)
finding.why: This is exactly what the no_color_literal_outside_theme custom_lint rule exists to catch, but custom_lint is currently broken (analyzer version mismatch, baselined separately) so nothing flags it today. stat_card.dart:89,104 duplicate AppColors.blueNavy's exact hex (0xFF03174C) as an inline literal instead of referencing it; preference_list_tile.dart:79 and preference_segmented_tile.dart:90 independently hardcode the identical 0xFF929BAA. The concrete cost: a rebrand of AppColors.blueNavy or of the settings-tile subtitle grey silently misses these inline copies, producing a visibly inconsistent surface next time the palette shifts.
finding.recommendation: Promote the duplicated literals (0xFF03174C, 0xFF929BAA) to named AppColors constants and reference them from both files; name or fold the remaining one-off literals in stat_card.dart/preference_segmented_tile.dart/app_dialog.dart.
acceptance_criteria: grep for `Color(0xFF` in lib/core/widgets/ returns no matches for the 3 currently-duplicated values (0xFF03174C, 0xFF929BAA) once fixed.
Once custom_lint_core/analyzer versions are reconciled (tracked separately), no_color_literal_outside_theme passes clean on these files.

finding.title: Strengthen PinEntryWidget's error-styling test to assert the border color, not just decoration non-null
finding.why: The test 'should have error styling when error message is present' (pin_entry_widget_test.dart:206-225) only asserts `firstField.decoration != null`, which is unconditionally true — the widget always sets a decoration whether or not hasError is true (its own comment admits 'which we can't easily test'). But it can: pin_entry_widget.dart:266-268 picks the border colour from `theme.colorScheme.error` vs `.outline` based on hasError, and that colour is directly readable off `decoration.enabledBorder` without pixel-level rendering. If that branch were deleted or inverted, this test would keep passing — a real regression in the parent-PIN wrong-attempt affordance would ship with green CI.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite the assertion to read `(firstField.decoration!.enabledBorder as OutlineInputBorder).borderSide.color` and compare it against `theme.colorScheme.error` in the error case and `.outline` in a matching non-error case.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails red when pin_entry_widget.dart's hasError ternary at line 266-268 is temporarily reverted to always return theme.colorScheme.outline, proving it actually exercises the branch.

finding.title: Split the four hand-written account-feature files that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: All four are hand-written (no .g.dart/.freezed.dart) and 1.1x-2.5x over the 400-line cap. signup_screen.dart is the sharpest case: unlike sign-in, which has a dedicated, unit-testable SignInController Notifier, ALL of sign-up's business orchestration (cloud/local/Google branching, Firebase error-code mapping, offline fallback dialog) lives directly in _SignupScreenState's async methods — test/features/account/onboarding/presentation/screens/*_test.dart are all widget-pump tests; there is no unit-level test of the sign-up decision logic itself, because there is nothing to unit-test it against.
finding.recommendation: Extract a SignupController Notifier mirroring SignInController's shape out of signup_screen.dart. Split account_picker_screen.dart's _AccountTile/_DashedOutlineButton/_DashedRRectPainter into separate widget files. Split sign_in_controller.dart's offline-restore and post-sign-in-navigation helpers into focused collaborator classes.
acceptance_criteria: A Rule-0 line-count checker (grep/script over hand-written lib/**/*.dart excluding *.g.dart/*.freezed.dart, failing at >400 lines) is wired into make audit
signup_screen.dart's sign-up decision logic gains a unit test that does not require pumping the widget tree

finding.title: Extract the duplicated, inconsistently-patched _extractFirebaseCode helper into one shared function
finding.why: The same '_extractFirebaseCode' helper is copy-pasted across 4 files in this batch (plus a 5th in features/settings/presentation/screens/upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart, outside it) and the copies have drifted: sign_in_controller.dart's own comment documents that the original pattern `\[([a-z-]+)\]` fails to match Firebase's real `[plugin/code]` format (e.g. `[firebase_auth/wrong-password]`), silently degrading every mapped error to the generic 'Sign-in failed' message — and fixed it locally. magic_link_service.dart and upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart still carry that exact stale pattern, so an email-already-in-use or wrong-password condition surfacing through either of those paths still silently falls through to a generic error today.
finding.recommendation: Extract one shared helper (e.g. core/auth/firebase_error_code.dart, consistent with Rule 3's core/auth placement for Firebase-adjacent parsing) using sign_in_controller.dart's fixed pattern, and delete the other 4 copies (in and out of this batch).
acceptance_criteria: A unit test on the shared helper asserts it extracts the code from both '[code]' and '[plugin/code]' shapes
AG-4 duplicate-symbol grep no longer finds multiple _extractFirebaseCode definitions

finding.title: Cache the account list Future instead of constructing it fresh inside AccountPickerScreen.build()
finding.why: registry.getAllAccounts() is called directly inside `Widget build()`, which returns a brand-new Future object on every rebuild. FutureBuilder tracks futures by identity, so any unrelated rebuild of this ConsumerWidget (a ref.watch(accountDbFileNameProvider) change from switching accounts, a locale/theme change, or any ancestor rebuild) restarts the FutureBuilder into ConnectionState.waiting — flashing the loading spinner over the already-rendered account list and re-querying the device registry — the textbook 'Future-in-build' Flutter anti-pattern.
finding.recommendation: Hoist the fetch behind a FutureProvider/AsyncNotifier (e.g. deviceAccountsProvider watched via ref.watch), or convert to ConsumerStatefulWidget and cache the Future in State so its identity is stable across rebuilds.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test triggers an unrelated provider rebuild while AccountPickerScreen is mounted and asserts the list does not revert to the loading spinner and getAllAccounts() is not invoked a second time
